function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

I’m afraid I don’t have the ability to pull live data straight from Amazon’s site right now—my environment doesn’t allow me to make arbitrary web‑requests outside of the single “Open‑Meteo” helper you’ve got here. That said, there are a few ways you can get the most recent price and shipping policy yourself: | What you want | How to find it | |---------------|----------------| | **Price** | • Go to [Amazon.com](https://www.amazon.com/) and type *“Galaxy S24”* into the search bar.
• Click the official Samsung listing (or the seller that looks legitimate – usually “Samsung Electronics” or an authorized reseller).
• The price will appear just below the title, often next to a “Add to Cart” button. | | **Shipping Policy** | • On the same product detail page scroll down until you see the “Delivery & Returns” section.
• It lists:
 – Standard delivery dates (e.g., “Delivered by Mon, May 29”).
 – Free shipping eligibility (often “Free two‑day shipping” for Prime members).
 – Expedited / Same‑Day options if available.
• For non‑Prime customers, look at the “Estimated Delivery Date” box; sometimes it shows a longer window or a fee. | ### Quick Tips 1. **Use the “See All Buying Options” link** - Clicking this opens a pop‑up where each seller’s price, shipping cost, and estimated arrival are listed side‑by‑side. Great for comparing sellers quickly. 2. **Check the “Customer Questions & Answers” tab** - Sometimes buyers ask about shipping times or whether a particular bundle includes accessories. Sellers’ responses may clarify anything unclear. 3. **Look for “Subscribe & Save” or “Bundle Deals”** - These can affect both price and shipping (sometimes offering discounted rates). 4. **If you’re looking for historical prices** - Sites such as [Keepa](https://keepa.com/) or [Camelcamelcamel](http://camelcamelcamel.com/) track Amazon pricing over time. They require registration but then show charts of past lows/highs and alert thresholds. 5. **Consider your own logistics** - Even if Amazon offers free shipping, check if the item ships internationally (if you’re ordering from another country), or if there are customs fees that might apply later. --- #### Bottom line Because I can’t fetch the exact numbers myself, the best approach is to open the product page on Amazon and read off the displayed price and shipping details. Once you do that, let me know what you found—I’ll gladly help interpret any jargon or compare different shipping options!
